system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Each task is instantiated using a task template, which minimally specifies the required information for that task
system_prompt_style.note: Per-agent fixed system prompts exist (src/hyperagent/prompts/executor.py system_exec is a static string); task templates populated per task. Only the paper and one prompt file are available, no line-level renderer seen.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Equipped with IDE-like tools such asgo to definitionandcode search, it traverses codebases rapidly
env_context_strategy.note: get_tree_structure tool also available to agents; Zoekt search is a tool, not prompt injection.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: A lightweightLLM summarizer 2 compiles and condenses execution logs from child agents, ensuring minimal information loss.
context_compaction.note: Summarization of child-agent logs before return to Planner; per-observation truncation not verifiable in the bundle.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Tools provide succinct, LLM-interpretable out- put and are optimized for their roles in the SE process.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: When you write bash command code for action, put the code in a markdown code block with the language set to bash.
tool_call_format.note: Executor emits bash code blocks; other agents' parsers (stop sequence "\nObservation:" suggests ReAct text format) were not in the bundle.

tool_count.note: Tool definition files (src/hyperagent/tools/*.py) listed in tree but not included; paper lists ~8 tools (code search, go to definition, get all references, get all symbols, get tree structure, open file, repair editor, interactive shell).

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: use repair_code to replace ‘enable_server =False` to ‘enable_server = True’ in the __init__ function.
edit_primitive.note: auto repair editor applies patches with linting feedback and repairing (Table 6); exact argument format not in evidence.

tool_schema_source.note: Tool schema files not in bundle; paper defers to App. A.3 (not included).

protocol_standardization.note: No dependency file or full source grep available; LSP (multilspy) is present but is not an agent/tool protocol in the value list.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote:
Tasks are bro-
ken down into subtasks and published to specific queues. Child agents, such asNavigator,Editor,
andExecutorinstances, monitor these queues and process tasks asynchronously
loop_primitives.evidence_locator: paper (arXiv 2409.16299), section not given in excerpt
loop_primitives.note: Paper prose describes queue-based asynchronous processing; the main run loop of the repo is not in the excerpts, so react/plan_execute could not be verified. Section number of the quote is not stated in the bundle.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Thought : “server setting does not appear when interface is triggered” Request : “Asks the Navigator to search for the keyword ‘server’ in the codebase.
planning_granularity.note: Plans exist as Planner free-text thoughts/requests; no stored plan object shown.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Comprising four specialized agents (Planner, Navigator, Code Editor, and Executor), it manages the full lifecycle of SE tasks from conception to verification.
multi_agent_topology.note: Planner is central coordinator; Editor excluded in predict mode.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: This is achieved using an asynchronous communication model based on a distributed Mes- sage Queue.
delegation_mechanism.note: Paper claim; repo implementation of the queue not verified.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Since your terminal is not stateful, you need to keep track of the state of the terminal.

long_term_memory.note: No memory module/config surface in evidence.

self_verification.note: Repair editor gives linting feedback; test running is done by the Executor agent at Planner's request (agent-driven).

retry_policy.note: Pass@5 in evaluation implies sampling but no retry mechanism evidence.

rollback.note: Editor tool code not in bundle.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: generating plans, delegating subtasks, and processing feedback until task completion or a predefined iteration limit is reached.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: employing lightweight LLMs for tasks like navigation and more advanced models for code editing and execution
cost_controls.note: Per-role static model assignment in config (README config nav/edit/exec/plan); closest value is model_routing.

timeouts.note: Paper mentions 'exit timeout' errors but no timeout mechanism shown.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: since the Executor uses jupyter kernel named hyperagent to execute the code
execution_isolation.note: Dockerfile present in tree, not inspected.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: since the Executor uses jupyter kernel named hyperagent to execute the code
filesystem_access.note: Relative to host subprocess; no scoping evidence.

permission_model.note: Tool execution code not in bundle.

tracing.note: Paper analyses trajectories but logging code not in bundle.

target_domain.evidence_quote: HyperAgent is a generalist multi-agent system designed to tackle a wide spectrum of software engineering (SE) tasks across various programming languages.
target_domain.note: arXiv:2608.02650 is an unrelated same-name AppWorld system, excluded.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: An advantage of our design is the ability to select the most suitable LLMs for each agent type
model_agnostic.note: README config uses api_type per role; open and closed models used.

first_release_date.note: No tag/first-commit info; paper arXiv:2409.16299 v1 date not in evidence.

stars.note: Date of star count not stated.
